sections.body: Incoming materials may include logs, boards, veneer sheets, or other items used in the process. Lot numbers and origin markings link materials to the production plan. At receipt, workers check the quantity, dimensions, visible damage, and documents; unidentified material must not be mixed with a verified lot.
sections.title: Work Concepts and Standards

sections.body:
Use the marked receiving area and match each marking to the work documents. If the quantity differs, a label is missing, or the wood is split, record what you observe and separate it as directed. Do not guess the type or copy a number from a neighboring stack.

Practice case: A stack of boards has no label, but a worker is asked to move it to the production-material area.
Recommended response: Separate the stack, record its location, and ask the person in charge to trace its identity before it is moved.

sections.body: Wood has grain patterns, growth rings, moisture content, and natural variation. Cracks, loose knots, warping, or surface changes can affect processing and quality. Workers inspect against product samples and criteria; final grading or decisions about use follow the designated procedure and role.
sections.title: Work Concepts and Standards

sections.body:
Inspect the material's surfaces and ends before processing, then mark or separate visible defects. If the grain or dimensions make cutting inconsistent with the instructions, stop and ask for guidance. Do not conceal a defect by turning the affected side inward in the stack.

Practice case: A board to be processed has a long crack at one end, but the documents do not say whether it is acceptable.
Recommended response: Set the board aside and ask quality-control staff to check it against the criteria before processing.

sections.body: Moisture content affects wood weight, dimensional stability, processing, and quality. Drying follows the schedule and target for each type and product; workers must not use a single figure for all wood. Stacking methods, air circulation, protection from water, and location records also help preserve material condition.
sections.title: Work Concepts and Standards

sections.body:
Check the stack label and drying instructions, use the measuring tool as trained, and record the actual result and time. Arrange spacers or supports as shown so the stack is stable and air can circulate. If the result is outside the target or the stack is wet or leaning, mark it and report the issue.

Recommended response: Repeat the check only as instructed, record the reading, and hold the transfer until the person in charge evaluates the result.

sections.body: Woodworking and sawing machines have hazardous blades, rollers, conveyors, and pinch points. Initial checks confirm guards are fitted, the area is clear of loose objects, and controls work according to the checklist. Only trained operators may run, clean, or clear jams under facility procedures.
sections.title: Work Concepts and Standards

sections.body:
Before starting, match the machine and task to the instructions, check guards and warning signs, and make sure other workers are in safe positions. If the sound, vibration, or guard is abnormal, do not start the machine. Never reach inside to clear sawdust while the machine is moving.

Practice case: A conveyor guard does not close fully, but the next operator has already prepared wood to feed into it.
Recommended response: Hold the feed, keep people away from the hazard, and report the guard for inspection before using the machine.

objectives: Memastikan tanda produk, spesifikasi, grade yang telah ditetapkan, dan jumlah cocok sebelum hasil dipindahkan.
Memilih tindakan aman pada satu situasi kerja dan menjelaskan alasannya.

lessons.response: Hold the bundle in the inspection area, record any visible lot number, and ask quality-control staff to restore its identity.
lessons.scenario: The grade label on a bundle is wet and illegible before the bundle enters the dispatch area.

sections.body: Product markings may show type, dimensions, grade, lot, or customer destination. Grade criteria come from specifications and designated inspections; workers must not guess a grade from appearance alone. Keep the wood-lot identity attached as it moves from processing to inspection, storage, or dispatch.
sections.title: Work Concepts and Standards

sections.body:
Compare the label with the documents after processing and before transfer. If a marking comes off, is damaged, or the quantity does not match, hold the lot and record its location and any readable information. Do not reprint a label or change the grade without authorization.

Practice case: The grade label on a bundle is wet and illegible before the bundle enters the dispatch area.
Recommended response: Hold the bundle in the inspection area, record any visible lot number, and ask quality-control staff to restore its identity.

modules.description: Keep wood products stable and identifiable during storage, transfer, and handover to the next process.

lessons.caution: Do not stand or work beneath a stack that appears to be shifting.

checks.explanation: An unstable bundle can collapse; keep people away and have the assigned person handle it.
options: Stop adding to the stack and keep people away from the collapse area
Brace the stack with your shoulder
Climb up and pull the board
Keep adding timber to balance the stack
checks.prompt: What is the safe response to a leaning timber stack?

checks.explanation: Do not brace the load with your body; stop work, keep a safe distance, and call for assistance.
options: Stop adding to the stack, keep people clear of its fall path, and ask the operator or supervisor to stabilize it using the appropriate procedure.
Bypass the guard or put a hand into a moving machine
Guess the dimensions, grade, or destination based on another product
Continue processing even though the material identity is unclear
checks.prompt: At work, a stack of boards begins to lean after one support shifts, while a worker is about to place another board on top. What is the most appropriate action?

checks.explanation: Sequence taught: Check the floor and stack supports → Confirm the identity and stacking direction are correct → Stack only up to the specified height → Keep people clear and report unstable bundles.
options: Check the floor and stack supports
Stack only up to the specified height
Keep people away and report the unstable bundle
Confirm the identity and stacking direction are correct
checks.prompt: In the “Stacking and bundle stability” workflow, what should be done next after the first step is complete?

dialogue.japanese: この束が傾いています。近づかないでください。
dialogue.meaning: This bundle is leaning. Do not come close.
dialogue.reading: このたばがかたむいています。ちかづかないでください。

dialogue.japanese: 作業を止めて、責任者を呼びます。
dialogue.meaning: I am stopping work and calling the person in charge.
dialogue.reading: さぎょうをとめて、せきにんしゃをよびます。

objectives: Menyusun kayu sesuai batas tumpukan dan menggunakan penyangga serta area simpan yang ditetapkan.
Memilih tindakan aman pada satu situasi kerja dan menjelaskan alasannya.
Menggunakan ungkapan Jepang sederhana untuk meminta konfirmasi atau melaporkan keadaan.
lessons.response: Stop adding boards, keep people clear of the fall path, and ask the operator or lead to stabilize the stack using the proper procedure.
lessons.scenario: A stack of boards starts leaning after one support shifts, while a worker is about to place another board on top.

sections.body: Wood stacks can collapse or shift if the surface is uneven, supports are misaligned, or the stack is too high. Stack limits and strapping methods follow workplace instructions. Keep hands and feet away from pinch points and never climb a stack; use suitable equipment operated by authorized personnel for transfers.
sections.title: Work Concepts and Standards

sections.body:
Check the floor, supports, labels, and stacking direction before adding wood. If a bundle leans, a strap is damaged, or wood shifts, keep people away and report it. Do not try to hold a heavy bundle with your body or rearrange a stack while equipment is moving.

Practice case: A stack of boards starts leaning after one support shifts, while a worker is about to place another board on top.
Recommended response: Stop adding boards, keep people clear of the fall path, and ask the operator or lead to stabilize the stack using the proper procedure.

Pastikan identitas serta arah susunan benar
Susun hanya pada batas tinggi yang ditetapkan
Jauhkan orang dan laporkan bundel tidak stabil

lessons.caution: Do not change a destination label to conceal an order shortage.

checks.explanation: This check confirms that the batch is correct, safe to transport, and going to the right customer.
options: The number of bundles, dimensions, labels, ties, and destination
Vehicle color alone
The driver's name without the order list
The stack that is easiest to reach
checks.prompt: What should be checked before loading timber onto a vehicle?

checks.explanation: The destination label differs. Hold the bundle and trace it before loading the vehicle.
options: Bypass the guard or put a hand into a moving machine
Hold the bundle and check its lot number against the order and production record before loading.
Guess the dimensions, grade, or destination based on another product
Continue processing even though the material identity is unclear

checks.explanation: Sequence taught: Read the order and destination identity → Count the bundles and check product dimensions → Inspect the ties and labels after packing → Confirm the destination before loading.
options: Count the bundles and check the product dimensions
Read the order and destination identity

Confirm the destination before loading

objectives: Mencocokkan jumlah, ukuran, label pelanggan, dan kondisi ikatan sebelum kayu dikirim.

lessons.response: Hold the bundle and match its lot number to the order and production records before loading.
lessons.scenario: A bundle has the correct dimensions, but its label shows a different customer from the loading list.

sections.body: Stack and strap wood products according to order dimensions, transport method, and facility rules. Keep destination labels readable after packaging. Checking the quantity and straps helps prevent shipping errors and falling wood during transfer; hold wood with mismatched identity before loading.
sections.title: Work Concepts and Standards

sections.body:
Use the order list, check the quantity and bundle number, inspect the straps and edge protectors, and place the products in the correct dispatch lane. Do not move products to a vehicle until the destination is confirmed. If a bundle is short or customer labels are mixed up, hold it in the dispatch area and report the issue.

Practice case: A bundle has the correct dimensions, but its label shows a different customer from the loading list.
Recommended response: Hold the bundle and match its lot number to the order and production records before loading.

steps: Baca pesanan dan identitas tujuan
Hitung bundel serta cocokkan ukuran produk
Periksa ikatan dan label setelah dikemas
Konfirmasi tujuan sebelum memuat

options: Bypass the guard or put a hand into a moving machine
Guess the dimensions, grade, or destination based on another product
Keep clear of the risk area, follow the facility's stop procedure or signals, and promptly inform the supervisor before handover.
Continue processing even though the material identity is unclear

Mark and report the abnormal machine condition

objectives: Membersihkan area sesuai tugas, melaporkan keausan alat atau kebocoran, dan menyerahkan status mesin serta lot.
Memilih tindakan aman pada satu situasi kerja dan menjelaskan alasannya.

lessons.response: Keep clear of the risk area, follow the shutdown procedure or facility signage, and notify the lead promptly before handover.
lessons.scenario: At the end of the shift, a worker notices a small leak near a machine and is unsure whether the line must be stopped.

sections.body: Handle sawdust, offcuts, and dust according to the designated schedule and method to keep routes and equipment clear. Clean machinery only under the required conditions and within your authority, following isolation procedures when needed. Shift reports record machines needing attention, held materials, and unfinished tasks.
sections.title: Work Concepts and Standards

sections.body:
Use designated cleaning tools and do not blow sawdust in a way that spreads it across the work area. If a guard, blade, or cable appears damaged, post a sign as required and notify the lead. Before leaving, hand over the status and location of the issue with the machine and lot numbers.

Practice case: At the end of the shift, a worker notices a small leak near a machine and is unsure whether the line must be stopped.
Recommended response: Keep clear of the risk area, follow the shutdown procedure or facility signage, and notify the lead promptly before handover.
